name: University of Wisconsin–Madison
character: The main campus sits on an isthmus along Lake Mendota with an urban street grid, a central hill, and buildings in Federal, Neoclassical, Romanesque, Gothic, Beaux-Arts, and Brutalist styles.

landmarks.name: Lake Mendota
landmarks.quote: The 933-acre (378 ha) main campus is located on the shores of Lake Mendota
landmarks.look: Broad lake bordering the campus shore, with sailboats on the water.

landmarks.name: Bascom Hall
landmarks.quote: Bascom Hall, at the top of Bascom Hill, is often considered the "heart of the campus."
landmarks.look: Historic hilltop hall with a balustrade, without a dome.

landmarks.name: Bascom Hill
landmarks.quote: Bascom Hall, at the top of Bascom Hill, is often considered the "heart of the campus."
landmarks.look: Central campus hill topped by historic university buildings.

landmarks.name: Memorial Union
landmarks.quote: The hub of campus life is the Memorial Union.
landmarks.look: Lakeside student union building with a terrace overlooking Lake Mendota.

landmarks.name: Carillon Tower
landmarks.quote: The Carillon Tower, erected in 1936, was designed by Warren Powers Laird and Paul Philippe Cret
landmarks.look: Tall bell tower with a balustrade echoing Bascom Hall.

landmarks.name: Henry Mall
landmarks.quote: Henry Mall is a 50-foot wide and 575-foot long landscaped quadrangle
landmarks.look: Long, narrow landscaped quadrangle lined with historic academic buildings and a boulder.

landmarks.name: Science Hall
landmarks.quote: Henry C. Koch designed the new Science Hall (built in 1888) in a Romanesque Revival style.

landmarks.name: Allen Centennial Gardens
landmarks.quote: It also features the Allen Centennial Gardens and University of Wisconsin–Madison Lakeshore Nature Preserve.
